about: The dust a supply rocket's engine throws off the landing pad as it comes down, as the game 2099 draws it (SupplyRocketView): a flat sheet of fine grains racing out along the ground every way round, barely lifted, falling back under the Moon's pull with no air to hold it. The landing pad is the scene record's; the rocket, built in code in the game, is not on the stage, nor its engine's glow. Real footage checked: the Apollo landing films (Apollo 11 and 12 descent, 16 mm) show the engine's blast as a sheet of dust streaming outward close to the ground, with no billowing cloud, and the Apollo 16 film shows the grains as a veil (2099's #116).
